business_problem: Fraudsters are using AI to find vulnerabilities, adapt tactics, and scale attacks across more payment channels, while traditional transaction-by-transaction controls struggle to catch coordinated fraud and authorized scam payments early enough.
solution_summary: Mastercard describes an in-house fraud prevention approach that uses generative AI and broader AI techniques to connect signals that appear low risk when viewed separately. The implementation ingests payment transaction activity along with contextual inputs including location, purchase frequency, transaction value, spending history, device information, account behavior, merchant onboarding signals, digital footprints, and cyber threat intelligence. AI correlates those signals across accounts, devices, merchants, and transactions to surface subtle anomalies, coordinated fraud networks, and scam manipulation patterns that rules-based checks may miss. The resulting risk insights are delivered to issuers and financial institutions so they can intervene earlier, reduce false declines, identify risky merchants before broader ecosystem exposure, and stop scam payments before money leaves an account. The source does not name specific storage platforms or commercial product brands.
data_flow: Mastercard combines payments intelligence, cyber threat intelligence, merchant onboarding signals, digital footprints, and transaction, account, behavioral, device, and location data. Its AI analyzes connections across accounts, devices, merchants, and transactions to score fraud and scam risk, then surfaces early warnings to issuers and financial institutions so they can block fraud, detect risky merchants, or intervene before funds leave an account.
business_outcome: Mastercard says the approach helps issuers detect more fraud while reducing false declines, identifies merchant and scam risk earlier, and gives financial institutions a chance to intervene before harm occurs, supporting safer digital commerce.
